The garage door groaned as Mara heaved it open, releasing a cloud of dust and the faint smell of motor oil. Her brother Tom stood beside her, hands in his pockets, staring at the shelves crammed with jars of screws and half-empty paint cans.

"I didn't realize he kept all this," Tom said quietly.

"He kept everything," Mara replied, running her fingers over a dusty workbench. "Remember how he used to say that nothing was ever truly broken, just waiting to be fixed?"

Tom let out a soft laugh. He reached for a battered toolbox on the lowest shelf and lifted the lid. Inside, tucked beneath a tangle of wrenches, was a small wooden bird, unfinished, its wings only half carved.

"Look at this," he whispered.

Mara took it from him and turned it over gently in her hands. The wood was smooth where their father's thumb must have rested countless times. For a moment neither of them spoke. Then Mara placed the bird carefully in the box marked keep, and together they got back to work.
